question: The Wardha is a tributary of which of the following rivers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Godavari river**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Wardha River is one of the major tributaries of the **Godavari River**.
 
• The confluence of the Wardha River with the Wainganga River forms the Pranahita River, which eventually joins the Godavari River.
 
• The Godavari River is the second longest river in India after the Ganges and is often referred to as the 'Dakshina Ganga' or the South Ganges.
 
• The Godavari River basin is one of the largest river basins in India, covering several states including Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, and Odisha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Godavari River**

 
 
• The Godavari River is the longest river in peninsular India and is revered as a sacred river in Hinduism.
 
• It originates from Trimbakeshwar in the Nashik district of Maharashtra.
 
• The river flows eastward for about 1,465 kilometers before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The Godavari basin is rich in biodiversity and supports a wide range of flora and fauna.
 
 
 
• **Wardha River**
 
 
• The Wardha River originates from the Satpura Range in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It flows southward through the states of Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.
 
• The river is known for its fertile plains which are used extensively for agriculture.
 
• The Wardha River is also important for its hydropower projects and irrigation facilities.
 
 
 
• **Wainganga River**
 
 
• The Wainganga River is another major tributary of the Godavari River.
 
• It originates from the Mundara village in Seoni district of Madhya Pradesh.
 
• The river flows through Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra before merging with the Wardha River to form the Pranahita River.
 
• The Wainganga River basin is known for its rich mineral resources and dense forests.
